title: Celebrity profile melts one cache node
description: A social app caches user profiles in a 20-node Redis cluster with cache-aside and a 10-minute TTL. When a celebrity goes viral, one Redis node hits 100% CPU serving a single key while the other 19 nodes are mostly idle, and database load stays normal. What is the most effective fix?

options.text: Add 20 more Redis nodes so the cluster has more total capacity.
options.explanation: The key still hashes to one node; more nodes do not spread a single key's traffic.

options.text: Add read replicas to the primary database.
options.explanation: The database is not the bottleneck; the hot cache node is. Replicas do not touch the cache path.

options.text: Replicate the hot key under several suffixed keys (or keep it in a short-TTL in-process cache on each API server) so its reads spread across nodes.
options.explanation: A hot key is a per-key problem. Spreading copies across shards or serving it from local memory removes the single-node bottleneck, at the cost of a few seconds of extra staleness.

options.text: Lower the TTL to 10 seconds so the key refreshes more often.
options.explanation: A shorter TTL increases misses and stampede risk without reducing the reads landing on that node.
